findings_to_judge.finding: FY26 has declined at a remarkably steady rate (-11.1% Q1, -9.5% Q2, -11.6% Q3; nine months $1,210.4m, -10.3%), yet the -10%/-12% full-year guide implies Q4 revenue of $272.9m-$306.6m against a $336.6m Q4 FY25 base, i.e. -8.9% to -18.9%: simple extrapolation of the year's own run-rate lands ~$300m, at the favourable end, while a $1.50bn full-year consensus requires ~$290m (-14%), a 3-4pp step-down no quarter of FY26 has produced.

The short base has not moved all year while the ability to exit has collapsed: short interest was 8,419,051 shares (27.5% of float) on 30 April 2026 and 7,754,157 (25.3%) on 14 August 2026, but days-to-cover went from 4.33 to 48.96 as average volume fell to ~200k/day, and the option chain offers no exit either (6,544 contracts total open interest, put/call OI 0.61, ATM bid-ask 67% of mid).

At the identical print one year ago the company explicitly declined to give numerical FY2026 guidance, framing the year instead as 'a pivotal period of foundation setting', and on the May 2026 call management again declined to provide any FY2027 numbers while noting the $12-13m of consultant costs expire 30 June.

The May 2025 credit-agreement amendment that replaced the leverage and fixed-charge tests with a minimum-liquidity covenant runs out at the fiscal quarter ending 27 December 2026, at which point the ratio covenants snap back, and the same amendment cut revolver commitments to $205m with a seasonal reduction to $125m — or $50m during the 'Affected Period' — from 1 January to 1 July each year; the FY26 10-K filed with this print has to speak to compliance across that snapback.
